title: Egg omelet with cheese and dark‑green vegetables, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet prepared without added fat, enriched with cream cheese and dark‑green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, kale). Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while the vegetables add vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs contain all essential amino acids in optimal proportions.
Cream cheese adds calcium and a modest amount of fat, but in moderate amounts it does not significantly raise the dish’s calorie count.
Dark‑green vegetables are rich in lutein and zeaxanthin, supporting eye health.
Cooking without oil preserves the natural flavors of the ingredients and reduces total calories.
Traditional omelets are often fried in butter, whereas this recipe relies on the egg’s own fat.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: One serving provides about 6 g of complete protein, helping maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply vitamin B12, riboflavin, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D from cheese
items.content: Cream cheese contributes calcium for bone health and a small amount of vitamin D.

items.title: Antioxidants from green vegetables
items.content: Lutein, zeaxanthin, and vitamin K support vision and cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low added‑fat content
items.content: Omitting oil reduces overall calories and saturated fat intake.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs or milk proteins may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium in cheese
items.content: Cream cheese can be salty, so choose a low‑sodium version if you need to limit salt intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat the eggs with a splash of water, stir in grated cream cheese and finely chopped green vegetables. Pour the mixture into a pre‑heated non‑stick pan and cook over medium heat, gently lifting the edges until the omelet sets. Serve immediately.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The omelet is best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a non‑stick pan without adding oil.
